notes: GPUI PANEL. The target UI framework is GPUI 0.2.2 (Zed's framework), not React, and you have no training knowledge of its exact API. Before writing, read: the finished panel crates as worked examples (rever-ui-traffic, rever-ui-history: their src and examples/preview.rs show how views, listeners, hover, scrolling, text fields, theme, strings and previews are done here), every file in rever-ui-kit/src, and vendor/gpui/src/elements/*.rs plus vendor/gpui/examples/*.rs for exact method names. Build a view struct implementing gpui::Render that reproduces the React component's layout, sizes, colors and behaviors (endpoints grouped by host and path template, method badges, counts, expanding a group, filtering, selecting an endpoint, any SVG it draws). The endpoint grouping logic the panel shows is already ported in rever-analysis (endpoints, endpoint_template): use it as a path dependency and read traffic from `Arc<Mutex<rever_core::traffic::TrafficStore>>` with a `refresh` method the host calls. Actions the panel cannot carry out itself (open a request, send to chat) are emitted as GPUI events. Colors and sizes come from src/renderer/src/styles.css (tokens in rever_ui_kit::theme::Theme; define a missing one locally and list it). User-facing strings go through `rever_ui_kit::i18n::Lang::t(key)` with the keys the TSX uses. Keep logic in plain functions with Korean-named unit tests; the file gets the `Port of` marker only when its behaviors are all there. Preview: fill examples/preview.rs so `cargo run -p rever-ui-apimap --example preview_apimap` shows the panel with fixture traffic; capture with `scripts/capture-window.sh preview_apimap /tmp/preview_apimap.png`, read the PNG, compare with the TSX, fix what is off. Do not bring windows to the front, do not capture the screen any other way, do not run the `rever` app, and never run cargo without `-p` (other crates in the workspace are mid-edit).
